slides.texte_overlay:
How to stop feeling awkward
on a first date
(and actually enjoy it)
Pick a place you know. Your coffee spot, a bar you like, a walk you've done a hundred times. When you're comfortable with the place, you've got one less thing to be nervous about.
Plan something to do, not just somewhere to sit. Mini golf, a market, a museum. "Want to check out the flea market Sunday?" Doing something side by side takes the pressure off.
Admit you're a little nervous. "Honestly, I was kind of nervous about this." Saying it out loud kills most of it, and it's usually a relief for her too, because she probably feels the same way.
Bring a little curiosity with you. Five minutes a day of history, art or science gives you stories nobody expects. "Did you know flamingos are pink because of what they eat?" Instant smile.
slides.texte_sophia: Bring a little curiosity with you. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. You'll have stories nobody expects on a first date.

slides.texte_overlay: Order something you actually want. Don't stress about looking cool with the menu. "I'm getting the burger, no regrets." Being easy and decisive about small things makes the whole date feel lighter.
Sit side by side at the bar instead of face to face at a table. It feels less like an interview, you both get to watch the room, and it's way easier to talk and laugh without staring at each other.
Text her after, but keep it short. "Had a great time tonight, get home safe." No essay, no games, no waiting three days. Being clear and kind is way less awkward than overthinking every word.
